claims.text: The scheduled pickup was 07:30 and the trip record's own derived driver_deadline sets the driver's latest permissible arrival at 07:35:00, returning arrived_by_deadline false with driver_late_after_scheduled_sec 300 (POL-NS-24); the rider cancelled at 07:37:40, after that deadline, so the driver failed to arrive in time and the rider's no-charge cancellation right under POL-NS-24 is engaged, and the whole 5.00 SGD fee must be refunded in full.

The GPS arrival test is not merely unmet for want of data: arrival_check returns corroborated false, arrived_at null and nearest_fix null, while the same trace is admissible at full weight and complete (50 fixes, 100% coverage, no gaps, maximum interval 30 s against an expected 30 s), so the failure to place the driver at the pickup within the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius is a substantive finding about this trip, not an artefact of a sparse trace.

POL-NS-21 runs the free wait from the scheduled time only where the driver arrived before it; otherwise it runs from the driver's arrival, and the free_wait block returns starts_at null, ends_at null and cancelled_after_free_wait null. The free wait therefore never began, so there was no expired wait for the no-show machinery of POL-NS-22 to act upon and no basis on this record for a 5.00 SGD no-show fee.

The fee was applied to a cancellation by the rider, not by the driver: the trip record's status is CANCELLED_BY_RIDER with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_CANCELLED, and POL-NS-22 charges the no-show fee where the driver cancels after the free wait; the condition that clause states is not shown on this record, so the fee was charged outside the clause that authorises it.

The fare ledger shows a single 5.00 SGD cancellation-fee line charged at 07:37:44 against payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and refund_if_voided_sgd is 5.00; the rider is therefore currently out of pocket the entire contested amount, so the correct outcome on that state is FULL_REFUND of all 5.00 SGD under POL-GEN-03, not a partial refund and not a restored charge.

The driver's only explanation is a jam on Sembawang Road, but the traffic-advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-05055-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, and POL-GEN-02(3) provides that a missing artifact carries no fact; nothing in the record therefore corroborates the jam, and POL-NS-24 contains no traffic exception that would excuse a failure to arrive by the deadline in any event.

POL-GEN-26 does not require escalation here: the fact POL-NS-24 turns on - whether the driver arrived by 07:35 - is answered by the trip record's driver_deadline block and corroborated by a complete 50-fix trace, and the only missing artifact is the traffic advisory, which carries no fact for either party (weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT); no fact this version needs is left open.

The rider does not rest this case on POL-NS-23, and says so plainly: the record shows the driver messaged at 07:31:10 and placed an answered 40 s in-app call at 07:33:20, both before the 07:37:40 cancellation, so the contact obligation is met on this record. That concession does not touch POL-NS-24, which obliges the driver to arrive rather than to telephone, and which the driver did not satisfy.

claims.text: The driver discharged the contact obligation POL-NS-23 imposes before the trip could be treated as a no-show. The chat log carries an in-app message from the driver at 07:31:10 (MSG-05055-001, 'Sorry ah got jam at Sembawang Road, another 5 min'), and the trip record carries an in-app call the driver placed at 07:33:20 that the rider answered and that lasted 40 seconds. Both precede the rider's 07:37:40 cancellation. POL-NS-23 voids the fee only where the message or the call is missing; neither is missing here, so the fee cannot be voided on the contact ground.

POL-NS-24's second limb does not bite. The 5.00 SGD goodwill credit is payable only where the driver 'also failed to attempt contact' — and the record shows the opposite: two in-app messages (07:31:10 and 07:36:30) and an answered 40-second in-app call (07:33:20), all before the 07:37:40 cancellation. No goodwill credit arises on this record.

The amount charged is exactly the fee POL-NS-22 prescribes, and no more. The payments ledger shows a single cancellation-fee line of 5.00 SGD charged at 07:37:44, reconciles to a 5.00 SGD total, and the derived money check records fee_matches_policy true against a policy fee of 5.00 SGD. That fee is the driver's compensation for time and fuel, and the driver spent both on this job: the driver-device trace runs 2.448 km between the first fix at 07:13:10 and the cancellation at 07:37:40.

The trace shows a driver working the job, not a driver who failed to show. The driver-device trace is complete — 50 fixes, 100% coverage, no gap longer than 30 seconds — and its fixes report the driver moving toward the pickup at 5–11 km/h through the approach and then stationary at the same position from 07:33:10 until the 07:37:40 cancellation, from which standstill he placed his answered 07:33:20 call. That is the signature of a vehicle ground down in the Sembawang Road congestion the driver reported, not of abandonment; the driver was still on the job and in contact when the rider cancelled.

No traffic record was attached for this trip, and the driver says so rather than presenting the advisory as though it existed: EV-ADVIS-05055-01 is MISSING with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and admissibility weight 0.0. Under POL-GEN-02 a missing artifact carries no fact, so the absent advisory cannot be weighed against the driver, and nothing in the record contradicts his contemporaneous account of the jam — an account the trace's very low reported speeds are consistent with.

On the charge as it stands, the outcome the driver seeks is the one POL-GEN-03 defines as NO_ACTION: the rider filed, the 5.00 SGD fee is charged and unrecovered (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.0), and preserving that present state leaves the fee standing. Nothing the rider has shown displaces the driver's compliance under POL-NS-23 or the correct fee under POL-NS-22.

ruling.explanation: Both parties: the rider filed over the 5.00 SGD no-show cancellation fee charged at 07:37:44 on 17 Aug 2026 for TRP-05055. The scheduled pickup was 07:30, so under POL-NS-24 the driver had to be at the pickup by 07:35. The trip record's own driver_deadline block (EV-TRIP-05055) returns arrived_by_deadline false with driver_late_after_scheduled_sec 300, and the complete 50-fix driver-device GPS trace (EV-GPS-05055, 100% coverage, no gap over 30 s, full weight 1.0) shows the driver still roughly 1.1 km from the pickup and stationary from 07:33:10 to the 07:37:40 cancellation, with arrival_check nearest_fix null and arrived_at null. The driver did not arrive by the deadline, and POL-NS-24 gives the rider the right to cancel at no charge, refunding the 5.00 SGD fee in full. Because the driver never arrived, POL-NS-21's free wait never began (free_wait starts_at and ends_at null), so POL-NS-22's condition for charging the fee - a driver cancellation after an expired free wait - was not met either; the fee was charged outside the clause that authorises it. The rider's claims on POL-NS-24, POL-NS-21 and POL-NS-22 are accepted and decide the case. The driver's claims that the contact obligation under POL-NS-23 was met (driver message 07:31:10, answered 40 s in-app call 07:33:20, both before the 07:37:40 cancellation) are accepted, and the rider concedes the same; that only shows the fee cannot be voided on the contact ground, it does not defeat POL-NS-24's arrival limb, which obliges the driver to arrive rather than to telephone. For that reason no 5.00 SGD goodwill credit arises under POL-NS-24 and no referral is produced. The driver's claim that the trace shows a driver diligently working the job is accepted as far as it goes but is not decisive: a driver stuck short of the pickup is still a driver who failed to arrive. The driver's claim of a Sembawang Road jam fails as an excuse: the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-05055-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, so under POL-GEN-02(3) it carries no fact, and in any event POL-NS-24 contains no traffic exception. The driver's POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION claim is rejected because the present state does not stand once the fee fails POL-NS-24. The amount charged is exactly the policy fee (fee_matches_policy true, 5.00 SGD), so POL-NS-22's fee-amount check produces no referral, and the rider's repeat-no-show counter under POL-NS-25 is not present and would not fire because the fee does not stand. No fact this version needs is left open, so POL-GEN-26 does not escalate. The dispute value is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and neither profile carries a fraud flag, so under POL-NS-26 the AI ruling is final. Outcome: the whole 5.00 SGD fee charged (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00) is refunded to the rider, with no driver compensation. Confidence 0.90: the deciding facts are carried by two independent artifacts (trip record and driver-device GPS trace), each at full weight 1.0.

ruling.explanation: This is the decision on TRP-05055, addressed to both parties. The rider booked a scheduled 07:30 pickup. Under POL-NS-24 the driver had to reach the pickup by 07:35 (07:30 plus 5 minutes). Two independent records, each at full weight (1.0), show he did not. The platform trip record records no arrival (arrived_at null; derived driver_deadline.arrived_by_deadline false against a deadline of 07:35:00 and driver_late_after_scheduled_sec 300). The driver-device GPS trace - complete, 50 fixes, 100% coverage, no gap above 30 s - puts the vehicle stationary roughly 1.1 km from the pickup from 07:33:10 until the 07:37:40 cancellation, with no fix inside the 50 m arrival radius (arrival_check.corroborated false, nearest_fix null). Because the driver did not arrive by the deadline, POL-NS-24 gives the rider the right to cancel at no charge and any fee charged is refunded in full. The 5.00 SGD cancellation fee charged at 07:37:44 (EV-FARE-05055; total_charged 5.00, refund_issued_sgd 0.00) is therefore refunded in full: FULL_REFUND of 5.00 SGD, with driver_compensation_sgd null. For the driver: the points in your favour are accepted but do not change the result. You did discharge POL-NS-23's contact obligation - your message at 07:31:10 and your answered 40-second in-app call at 07:33:20 both precede the 07:37:40 cancellation - so the fee is not voided on the contact ground; but meeting the contact obligation does not excuse the separate failure to arrive that POL-NS-24 addresses. The 5.00 SGD charged is the correct POL-NS-22 amount and the ledger reconciles, but a correct amount does not make payable a fee that POL-NS-24 requires be refunded. The Sembawang Road congestion you report, and the missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-05055-01 (weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT, carrying no fact either way), do not supply a traffic exception: POL-NS-24 contains none. No further adjustment follows. The driver did attempt contact, so POL-NS-24's 5.00 SGD goodwill credit does not arise; the rider profile does not carry no_show_cancellations_30d, so POL-NS-25's repeat no-show referral does not fire; the fee is exactly 5.00 SGD, so POL-NS-22's fee-amount referral does not fire. There is no safety flag and the value (5.00 SGD) is below 10.00 SGD, so the AI ruling is final and no escalation applies. Confidence is 0.95, above the 0.0 POL-NS-26 requires for a no-show of this value; the deciding fact is carried by two independent artifacts, the trip record and the GPS trace, both at weight 1.0.

Rider: your cancellation is upheld and the 5.00 SGD fee is returned in full. Your trip was scheduled for 07:30 (EV-TRIP-05055). Under POL-NS-21 the driver held a 5-minute free wait, so he was required at the pickup by 07:35:00, and POL-NS-24 gives you the right to cancel at no charge if he had not arrived by then, with any fee charged refunded in full. The record shows he had not: the trip record carries arrived_at null and its derived driver_deadline returns arrived_by_deadline false against the 07:35:00 deadline (EV-TRIP-05055), and the complete 50-fix driver trace (EV-GPS-05055, 100% coverage, maximum interval 30 s, no gaps) never places the vehicle within the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius (POL-NS-21) — its last fixes show the car stationary roughly a kilometre from the pickup from 07:33:10 until your 07:37:40 cancellation. You cancelled at 07:37:40, after the deadline the driver missed, so the 5.00 SGD charged at 07:37:44 (EV-FARE-05055) is refunded in full under POL-GEN-03.

Driver: your account of the Sembawang Road jam is considered, and your trace's very low reported speeds are consistent with congestion, but POL-NS-24 contains no traffic exception, and the traffic advisory you would rely on (EV-ADVIS-05055-01) is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, so under POL-GEN-02(3) it carries no fact. You did satisfy POL-NS-23's contact obligation — your 07:31:10 in-app message and the answered 40-second call placed at 07:33:20 both precede the cancellation (EV-CHAT-05055, EV-TRIP-05055) — so the fee is not voided on the contact ground, and no 5.00 SGD goodwill credit under POL-NS-24 arises, because that credit requires a failure to attempt contact, which the record disproves. Your POL-NS-22 point that the ledger charges exactly the 5.00 SGD policy fee is accurate but does not preserve it: POL-NS-22 authorises the no-show fee where the driver cancels after the free wait, and here the rider cancelled, so the fee falls to be refunded under POL-NS-24 rather than upheld. POL-GEN-26 does not require escalation: the fact POL-NS-24 turns on — whether the driver arrived by 07:35 — is answered by the trip record and the complete trace, and the only missing artifact carries no fact for either side.

No referral arises. The POL-NS-24 goodwill credit does not fire (contact was attempted); the POL-NS-22 fee-amount check does not fire (the fee is exactly 5.00 SGD); and the POL-NS-25 repeat no-show flag does not fire (the rider profile carries no no_show_cancellations_30d counter and this fee does not stand).

ledger.claim: The scheduled pickup was 07:30 and the trip record's own derived driver_deadline sets the driver's latest permissible arrival at 07:35:00, returning arrived_by_deadline false with driver_late_after_scheduled_sec 300 (POL-NS-24); the rider cancelled at 07:37:40, after that deadline, so the driver failed to arrive in time and the rider's no-charge cancellation right under POL-NS-24 is engaged, and the whole 5.00 SGD fee must be refunded in full.

The GPS arrival test is not merely unmet for want of data: arrival_check returns corroborated false, arrived_at null and nearest_fix null, while the same trace is admissible at full weight and complete (50 fixes, 100% coverage, no gaps, maximum interval 30 s against an expected 30 s), so the failure to place the driver at the pickup within the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius is a substantive finding about this trip, not an artefact of a sparse trace.

POL-NS-21 runs the free wait from the scheduled time only where the driver arrived before it; otherwise it runs from the driver's arrival, and the free_wait block returns starts_at null, ends_at null and cancelled_after_free_wait null. The free wait therefore never began, so there was no expired wait for the no-show machinery of POL-NS-22 to act upon and no basis on this record for a 5.00 SGD no-show fee.

The fee was applied to a cancellation by the rider, not by the driver: the trip record's status is CANCELLED_BY_RIDER with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_CANCELLED, and POL-NS-22 charges the no-show fee where the driver cancels after the free wait; the condition that clause states is not shown on this record, so the fee was charged outside the clause that authorises it.

The fare ledger shows a single 5.00 SGD cancellation-fee line charged at 07:37:44 against payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and refund_if_voided_sgd is 5.00; the rider is therefore currently out of pocket the entire contested amount, so the correct outcome on that state is FULL_REFUND of all 5.00 SGD under POL-GEN-03, not a partial refund and not a restored charge.

The driver's only explanation is a jam on Sembawang Road, but the traffic-advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-05055-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, and POL-GEN-02(3) provides that a missing artifact carries no fact; nothing in the record therefore corroborates the jam, and POL-NS-24 contains no traffic exception that would excuse a failure to arrive by the deadline in any event.

POL-GEN-26 does not require escalation here: the fact POL-NS-24 turns on - whether the driver arrived by 07:35 - is answered by the trip record's driver_deadline block and corroborated by a complete 50-fix trace, and the only missing artifact is the traffic advisory, which carries no fact for either party (weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT); no fact this version needs is left open.

The rider does not rest this case on POL-NS-23, and says so plainly: the record shows the driver messaged at 07:31:10 and placed an answered 40 s in-app call at 07:33:20, both before the 07:37:40 cancellation, so the contact obligation is met on this record. That concession does not touch POL-NS-24, which obliges the driver to arrive rather than to telephone, and which the driver did not satisfy.

The driver discharged the contact obligation POL-NS-23 imposes before the trip could be treated as a no-show. The chat log carries an in-app message from the driver at 07:31:10 (MSG-05055-001, 'Sorry ah got jam at Sembawang Road, another 5 min'), and the trip record carries an in-app call the driver placed at 07:33:20 that the rider answered and that lasted 40 seconds. Both precede the rider's 07:37:40 cancellation. POL-NS-23 voids the fee only where the message or the call is missing; neither is missing here, so the fee cannot be voided on the contact ground.

POL-NS-24's second limb does not bite. The 5.00 SGD goodwill credit is payable only where the driver 'also failed to attempt contact' — and the record shows the opposite: two in-app messages (07:31:10 and 07:36:30) and an answered 40-second in-app call (07:33:20), all before the 07:37:40 cancellation. No goodwill credit arises on this record.

The amount charged is exactly the fee POL-NS-22 prescribes, and no more. The payments ledger shows a single cancellation-fee line of 5.00 SGD charged at 07:37:44, reconciles to a 5.00 SGD total, and the derived money check records fee_matches_policy true against a policy fee of 5.00 SGD. That fee is the driver's compensation for time and fuel, and the driver spent both on this job: the driver-device trace runs 2.448 km between the first fix at 07:13:10 and the cancellation at 07:37:40.

The trace shows a driver working the job, not a driver who failed to show. The driver-device trace is complete — 50 fixes, 100% coverage, no gap longer than 30 seconds — and its fixes report the driver moving toward the pickup at 5–11 km/h through the approach and then stationary at the same position from 07:33:10 until the 07:37:40 cancellation, from which standstill he placed his answered 07:33:20 call. That is the signature of a vehicle ground down in the Sembawang Road congestion the driver reported, not of abandonment; the driver was still on the job and in contact when the rider cancelled.

No traffic record was attached for this trip, and the driver says so rather than presenting the advisory as though it existed: EV-ADVIS-05055-01 is MISSING with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and admissibility weight 0.0. Under POL-GEN-02 a missing artifact carries no fact, so the absent advisory cannot be weighed against the driver, and nothing in the record contradicts his contemporaneous account of the jam — an account the trace's very low reported speeds are consistent with.

On the charge as it stands, the outcome the driver seeks is the one POL-GEN-03 defines as NO_ACTION: the rider filed, the 5.00 SGD fee is charged and unrecovered (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.0), and preserving that present state leaves the fee standing. Nothing the rider has shown displaces the driver's compliance under POL-NS-23 or the correct fee under POL-NS-22.
